messages:
anya: quick sync — we need a short playbook for runtime pool lifecycle: warmup credits, graceful drain, and an explicit fallback path when dedicated capacity is exhausted. thoughts?

mason: +1. we keep hitting tail latency during scale spikes. main question: conservative prewarm (higher cost) vs reactive fast-provision (higher failure risk).

li: for some tenants we already have SLAs that require <100ms p95. prewarm seems necessary for those — but we should make it per-tenant and opt-in.

rami: agree with li. can we separate a "latency-tier" flag on tenant config that toggles prewarm tokens? that would avoid global overprovisioning.

anya: exactly what I was thinking. proposal: two orthogonal levers — (1) tenant latency-tier (on/off/burst) and (2) pool warmup-policy (aggressive/soft/none). map them when creating leases.

mason: implementation note: warmup means we need to hold a headroom reservation for GPU warmup time (30–90s). if headroom consumed, we should fallback to a queued soft-degradation path instead of immediate failure.

rami: fallback options: (a) route to compatible lower-capacity model variant, (b) route to shared-hosted with throttling, (c) return 503 with suggested retry-after. Prefer (a) then (b).

li: +1 for variant routing. but must ensure model-compatibility metadata exists. also need tracing to mark which fallback was used for billing and SLOs.

anya: operational playbook draft: 1) on lease request check tenant tier -> compute warmup requirement; 2) attempt immediate admission; 3) if admission fails and tenant allows variant, route to variant; 4) if variant not available but shared-hosted allowed, route there with throttling; 5) otherwise queue for prewarm with backoff and return 202 (accepted) to caller with telemetry tag.

mason: can we return structured response with fields: {admitted: bool, path: "dedicated|variant|hosted|queued", eta_seconds: int, trace_id: str}? clients can choose to present fallback UX.

sasha: deploy-bot: prod canary of this flow should start with 1% tenants and only non-critical latency-tier "burst" tenants. monitor cost and p95. :warning:

rami: observability: add metrics: fallback_count_by_tenant, routing_path_histogram, warmup_latency_ms, queue_time_seconds. also logging: emit lease_decision events. we need a dashboard with tenant filter.

li: small implementation detail: when we queue for prewarm, capture an idempotency token so repeated client retries don't spawn duplicate warmups. also persist minimal state to our lease store for 1h.

anya: good call re idempotency. followup: policy edgecases — what if warmup fails after billing begins? propose: refund unused warmup credits and mark tenant for automatic retry; escalate if failure rate > 5% in 10m window.

mason: prewarm costs: we should expose an estimation API: /v1/leases/estimate?model=...&seq=... returns expected_gpu_seconds and price. helps product and customers decide latency-tier.

rami: rollout plan: feature-flag the routing logic behind runtime.fallback_v2, enable telemetry-only first. create smoke tests that simulate sudden burst and validate fallback handoffs.

anya: can someone take patch to the lease-granting flow and add the structured response contract? mason?

mason: I'll take it. I'll add tests for variant routing and idempotency token behavior.

li: I'll add the metrics and dashboard draft.

rami: I'll own rollout plan + canary config. sasha can you schedule the canary?

sasha: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for next Tue 03:00 UTC, 1% tenants, monitor channels: #eng-runtime, #incidents. :white_check_mark:

anya: awesome. I'll write the short playbook doc and add examples of responses and client UX suggestions. thanks all.
